claims.text: The proposed approach combines CALPHAD-based high-throughput screening with machine-learning interatomic-potential simulations.
The integrated approach will reliably identify high-entropy alloys with low phonon thermal conductivity.
High-entropy alloys can exhibit atomic-scale lattice distortions because their constituent elements have different atomic sizes.
The predictive approach can selectively target alloy systems having high levels of lattice distortion.
The predictive approach can selectively target alloy systems having high levels of atomic mass disorder.
Atomic-scale lattice distortions act as effective phonon-scattering centers in high-entropy alloys.
Atomic mass disorder acts as an effective phonon-scattering mechanism in high-entropy alloys.
High configurational entropy produces significant local lattice strain.
High configurational entropy produces significant local mass fluctuations.
Lattice strain and mass fluctuations enhance phonon scattering and thereby lower phonon thermal conductivity.
The integrated approach will improve prediction accuracy by at least 20% relative to conventional empirical or first-principles methods.
Conventional empirical and first-principles approaches have lower accuracy in capturing lattice-distortion effects on phonon transport.
The approach is applicable only to stable, single-phase FCC or BCC high-entropy alloys.
Predictions may correlate poorly with experiments for multiphase alloys or alloys containing significant intermetallic precipitation.
Temperatures up to 900 °C are relevant to the intended thermal-insulation application.
Alloys selected by the integrated approach will have phonon thermal conductivity at least approximately 20% lower than alloys selected by conventional prediction methods.
Experimental thermal-conductivity measurements will match the integrated approach's computational predictions within acceptable error margins.
Processing conditions and microstructural inhomogeneities may affect the thermal-transport outcomes.
A laser-flash experiment can directly provide the phonon component of thermal conductivity.
Failure to obtain an approximately 20% conductivity reduction relative to baseline alloys is designated as a falsifying outcome.

contradictions.description: The boundary excludes alloys that form intermetallic or multiphase microstructures, whereas the falsification rule treats formation of those out-of-scope microstructures as falsification rather than as a failed domain assumption.

The hypothesis specifies at least 20% improvement in prediction accuracy, but the predicted outcome and falsification rule use at least 20% reduction in thermal conductivity. Prediction error and conductivity reduction are different quantities, so the benchmark does not directly test the stated accuracy claim.
